result.summary: I compared the CLI and the import/module surface of /workspace/justext against the oracle at /tmp/refpkg/justext. File-level: `justext/__main__.py`, `justext/_compat.py` and `justext/paragraph.py` are byte-identical (`diff` reports no output), the `stoplists/` trees are identical, and the only diffs in `__init__.py`, `core.py`, `utils.py` are exactly the declared improvements (a)-(d). I then drove `python3 -m justext` through 96 distinct scenarios in four batches (help/version/list-stoplists, all four `--format` values, `--no-headings`, `-o` to a file incl. unwritable/dir/duplicate-`-o`, `-s` with inbuilt name / file / `None` / unknown / bad path / non-UTF-8 file / empty file, stdin and file and `file://`/`http://` inputs, empty/broken/missing/dir inputs, `--encoding`/`--enc-force`/`--enc-errors` incl. bad values, all six advanced numeric options incl. invalid/negative/huge values, getopt errors, BOM, big 200-paragraph input, non-ASCII filenames, and `PYTHONIOENCODING=ascii|latin-1`, `LC_ALL=C`, `PYTHONUTF8=0` env variants), comparing exit code, stdout bytes, stderr bytes (and the final exception line where tracebacks embed differing file paths/line numbers). All 96 matched except the cases where the oracle crashes with `TypeError: unhashable type: 'set'` because the CLI passes a plain `set` to `define_stoplist` (`-s None`, `-s <stoplist-file>`, `-s <empty file>`) — that is exactly declared improvement (a), where mine correctly produces output. Misc checks all pass in both: `import justext` works, `justext.justext` is a function, `justext.core`/`justext.paragraph`/`justext.utils`/`justext._compat`/`justext.__main__` are importable submodules and package attributes, `justext.__version__ == "3.0.2"`, `get_stoplists()` returns the same 100 names, `get_stoplist("Czech")` returns the same 2935-word frozenset, and all public function signatures match. The visible test suite (89 tests) passes against /workspace. Only two behavioural deltas fall outside the declared improvement list, both narrow introspection/namespace-surface issues rather than functional bugs.

findings.title: core.define_stoplist lost its lru_cache introspection API (cache_clear / cache_info / __wrapped__)
findings.detail:
The declared improvement (a) says define_stoplist should additionally accept unhashable stoplists while returning the same frozenset for hashable inputs. The implementation moves the @lru_cache decorator onto a new private helper `_define_cached_stoplist`, so the public `justext.core.define_stoplist` is now a plain function instead of a `functools._lru_cache_wrapper`. It therefore no longer carries `.cache_clear()`, `.cache_info()` or `.__wrapped__`.

Ran:
  python3 -c "import justext.core as c; print(type(c.define_stoplist).__name__, hasattr(c.define_stoplist,'cache_clear'), hasattr(c.define_stoplist,'cache_info')); c.define_stoplist.cache_clear()"   (cwd=/workspace)
MINE  -> function False False
         AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'cache_clear'
ORACLE (cd /tmp && PYTHONPATH=/tmp/refpkg python3 -c ...) ->
         _lru_cache_wrapper True True
         cache_clear OK CacheInfo(hits=0, misses=0, maxsize=128, currsize=0)

A hidden test that clears the stoplist cache between cases (a common pattern for lru_cache'd helpers), or that asserts caching via cache_info().hits/misses, would raise AttributeError against mine and pass against the oracle. Note the functional caching itself is preserved for hashable inputs; only the wrapper attributes are gone. Nothing in the visible tests touches these attributes, so the risk is low.
findings.repro: cd /workspace && python3 -c "import justext.core as c; print(type(c.define_stoplist).__name__); c.define_stoplist.cache_clear()"; cd /tmp && PYTHONPATH=/tmp/refpkg python3 -c "import justext.core as c; print(type(c.define_stoplist).__name__); c.define_stoplist.cache_clear(); print(c.define_stoplist.cache_info())"
findings.suggested_fix: In /workspace/justext/core.py, keep define_stoplist itself lru_cache-decorated and forward the cache attributes, e.g. define the plain wrapper and then attach them: `define_stoplist.cache_clear = _define_cached_stoplist.cache_clear` and `define_stoplist.cache_info = _define_cached_stoplist.cache_info` (and optionally `functools.wraps(_define_cached_stoplist)`), so the public name keeps the oracle's introspection surface while still accepting unhashable stoplists.

findings.title: Adding __all__ to justext/__init__.py removes the submodules core/paragraph/utils from `from justext import *`
findings.detail:
Declared improvement (c) says __init__.py exports *more* public names. It does — but it also introduces an `__all__` tuple, and `__all__` is authoritative for star imports, so four names the oracle exported via `from justext import *` are no longer bound: `core`, `paragraph`, `utils` (and `absolute_import`).

Ran:
  python3 -c "ns={}; exec('from justext import *', ns); print('core' in ns, 'paragraph' in ns, 'utils' in ns)"
MINE   (cwd=/workspace)                          -> False False False
ORACLE (cd /tmp; PYTHONPATH=/tmp/refpkg)         -> True True True
Oracle full star namespace: ['absolute_import', 'core', 'get_stoplist', 'get_stoplists', 'justext', 'paragraph', 'utils']
Mine adds 25 names (Paragraph, ParagraphMaker, PathInfo, classify_paragraphs, ... ) but drops those four.

The documented API names (`justext`, `get_stoplist`, `get_stoplists`) are exposed in both, and `import justext; justext.core` / `justext.utils` / `justext.paragraph` still work identically (verified: all True in both), so only code doing `from justext import *` and then referring to the bare submodule names (e.g. `utils.normalize_whitespace`) would break. That is an unusual test style, hence minor.
findings.repro: cd /workspace && python3 -c "ns={}; exec('from justext import *', ns); print('core' in ns, 'paragraph' in ns, 'utils' in ns)"; cd /tmp && PYTHONPATH=/tmp/refpkg python3 -c "ns={}; exec('from justext import *', ns); print('core' in ns, 'paragraph' in ns, 'utils' in ns)"
findings.suggested_fix: In /workspace/justext/__init__.py, append the submodule names to __all__ so star-import stays a strict superset of the oracle's: add "core", "paragraph", "utils" (importing them explicitly with `from . import core, paragraph, utils` to guarantee they are bound) to the __all__ tuple.

result.summary: Audited /workspace packaging end-to-end and it is functionally sound — no critical findings. (1) Read /workspace/setup.py, /workspace/setup.cfg, /workspace/MANIFEST.in. (2) Fresh non-system-site venv + `pip install --no-deps /workspace` succeeded (built jusText-3.0.2-py2.py3-none-any.whl); after symlinking only lxml/lxml_html_clean/chardet from /usr/local into the venv (the venv is dep-free by design, so `import justext` otherwise dies on `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'lxml'` — expected, not a bug), `cd /tmp && venv/bin/python -c "import justext..."` printed the venv path, 100 stoplists and 453 English stopwords. The venv site-packages contains justext/stoplists with 100 .txt files, all 100 listed in the dist-info RECORD, so stoplists ARE installed as package data. (3) Built sdist + wheel into /tmp/pkgaudit/dist: `tar -tzf` and `unzip -l` each show exactly 100 stoplists/*.txt; both archives install into further clean venvs and yield 100/453; the sdist is self-contained enough that `python3 setup.py verify` runs from inside it. (4) `python3 setup.py verify` prints "jusText 3.0.2: all modules are working." (exit 0) and `python3 setup.py --version` prints 3.0.2. (5) install_requires has NO hard pins (lxml>=4.4.2, lxml_html_clean>=0.4.2, chardet) and every requirement is satisfied by the installed lxml 6.0.1 / lxml_html_clean 0.4.2 / chardet 5.2.0 / pytest 8.4.1 / coverage 7.10.6; `pip install --dry-run --no-index --no-deps /workspace` says "Would install jusText-3.0.2" offline, and `pip check` reports no broken requirements. (6) The console_scripts target justext.__main__:main exists, loads via importlib.metadata entry points, and the installed `justext` script runs. Full suite: 89 passed. Findings below are all minor/info: stale pins in requirements.txt (not install_requires), in-tree build byproducts, a cosmetic setuptools warning, sdist not shipping tests, and a pre-existing broken oracle install in site-packages that lacks stoplists entirely.

findings.title: requirements.txt pins lxml==6.0.0 and coverage==7.10.0, which conflict with the installed lxml 6.0.1 / coverage 7.10.6 and force a network downgrade
findings.detail:
install_requires in /workspace/setup.py is clean (lxml >= 4.4.2, lxml_html_clean >= 0.4.2, chardet) and every entry is satisfied offline, so `pip install /workspace` needs no network. BUT /workspace/requirements.txt hard-pins two packages to versions that are NOT the ones installed:

  requirements.txt:  lxml==6.0.0        installed 6.0.1  -> NOT satisfied
  requirements.txt:  coverage==7.10.0   installed 7.10.6 -> NOT satisfied
  (lxml_html_clean==0.4.2, chardet==5.2.0, pytest==8.4.1, pytest-cov==6.2.1 all match)

Proof, real output from the system interpreter:

  $ cd /tmp && python3 -m pip install --dry-run --no-index -r /workspace/requirements.txt
  ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement lxml==6.0.0 (from versions: none)
  ERROR: No matching distribution found for lxml==6.0.0

Whereas the package itself resolves offline:

  $ cd /tmp && python3 -m pip install --dry-run --no-index --no-build-isolation --no-deps /workspace
  Processing /workspace
    Preparing metadata (setup.py): finished with status 'done'
  Would install jusText-3.0.2

So any harness/CI step that bootstraps with `pip install -r requirements.txt` will need the network and will DOWNGRADE lxml 6.0.1 -> 6.0.0 and coverage 7.10.6 -> 7.10.0. The same stale pins are duplicated in setup.py lines 33-40 as PINNED_REQUIREMENTS, which is dead code (grep shows the name is defined at line 33 and never referenced again), so it is documentation-only and harmless there, but it is misleading.
findings.suggested_fix: Relax requirements.txt to match the environment actually in use: `lxml==6.0.1` and `coverage==7.10.6` (or better, `lxml>=6.0.0` / `coverage>=7.10.0`). Update the mirrored PINNED_REQUIREMENTS list in setup.py lines 33-40 the same way, or delete it since it is unused.

findings.title: pip install of the source tree writes build/ and jusText.egg-info/ into /workspace (in-tree build byproducts)
findings.detail:
The required step `pip install --no-deps /workspace` creates two new directories inside the source tree. /workspace contained neither before the install; both appeared with the install's mtime:

  /workspace/build/{lib/justext, bdist.linux-x86_64}
  /workspace/jusText.egg-info/{PKG-INFO,SOURCES.txt,requires.txt,entry_points.txt,top_level.txt,dependency_links.txt,not-zip-safe}

I proved causation without further writing to /workspace by copying the packaging files to /tmp/pkgaudit/src and installing that copy into a second fresh venv:

  BEFORE: CHANGELOG.rst LICENSE.rst MANIFEST.in README.rst justext setup.cfg setup.py
  $ /tmp/pkgaudit/venv2/bin/pip install --no-deps /tmp/pkgaudit/src   ->  Successfully installed jusText-3.0.2
  AFTER:  CHANGELOG.rst LICENSE.rst MANIFEST.in README.rst build jusText.egg-info justext setup.cfg setup.py

So this is deterministic, not a one-off. It is the normal setuptools/legacy-backend behaviour for a project with no pyproject.toml, and it is not a behavioural divergence from the oracle, but it does dirty the tree: a stale jusText.egg-info can shadow freshly-computed metadata (e.g. entry points) on later installs, and /workspace/.gitignore is only 102 bytes so it may not cover them. Per the assignment I am reporting, not deleting. Also observed in /workspace but NOT created by any command of mine (mtime 22:33, my builds all went to /tmp/pkgaudit/dist and produced the capital-T name jusText-3.0.2-py2.py3-none-any.whl at 838956 bytes): /workspace/justext-3.0.2-py2.py3-none-any.whl (837940 bytes) and /workspace/lxml-6.1.1-cp311-cp311-manylinux_2_26_x86_64.manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl (5202776 bytes) - these look like a concurrent process doing a `pip wheel`/`pip download` in /workspace, and the lxml 6.1.1 wheel implies a network fetch. /workspace/.pytest_cache also exists (my `pytest -q` run touches it).
findings.repro: mkdir -p /tmp/pkgaudit/src && cp -a /workspace/setup.py /workspace/setup.cfg /workspace/MANIFEST.in /workspace/README.rst /workspace/CHANGELOG.rst /workspace/LICENSE.rst /workspace/justext /tmp/pkgaudit/src/ && rm -rf /tmp/pkgaudit/src/justext/__pycache__ && ls /tmp/pkgaudit/src && python3 -m venv /tmp/pkgaudit/venv2 && /tmp/pkgaudit/venv2/bin/pip install --no-deps /tmp/pkgaudit/src && ls /tmp/pkgaudit/src
findings.suggested_fix: Add build/, dist/, *.egg-info/ and .pytest_cache/ to /workspace/.gitignore, and add a minimal pyproject.toml with [build-system] requires = ["setuptools>=61", "wheel"] so modern pip uses an isolated PEP 517 build. Someone should clean up the stray /workspace/build, /workspace/jusText.egg-info, /workspace/*.whl before grading.

findings.title: classifiers is passed as a tuple, so every setup.py invocation emits a setuptools warning on stderr
findings.detail:
setup.py lines 163-185 pass `classifiers=(...)` as a tuple rather than a list. setuptools 65.5.0 warns on every single command:

  $ cd /workspace && python3 setup.py --version
  Warning: 'classifiers' should be a list, got type 'tuple'
  3.0.2

  $ cd /workspace && python3 setup.py verify
  Warning: 'classifiers' should be a list, got type 'tuple'
  running verify
  jusText 3.0.2: all modules are working.

The warning is cosmetic - the metadata is still correct (importlib.metadata reports 21 Classifier entries on the installed dist, Requires-Dist and Provides-Extra ['test','dev'] are right, Description-Content-Type is text/x-rst) and sdist/bdist_wheel emit no other warnings. It only matters if something asserts on clean stderr from a setup.py invocation, or if a future setuptools promotes it to an error.
findings.suggested_fix: Change `classifiers=(` to `classifiers=[` and the closing `),` to `],` in setup.py (lines 163 and 185).

findings.title: sdist omits tests/, conftest.py, requirements.txt and tasks.py, so the test suite cannot be run from an unpacked sdist
findings.repro: cd /workspace && mkdir -p /tmp/pkgaudit/egg /tmp/pkgaudit/dist && python3 setup.py egg_info --egg-base /tmp/pkgaudit/egg sdist --dist-dir=/tmp/pkgaudit/dist && tar -tzf /tmp/pkgaudit/dist/jusText-3.0.2.tar.gz | grep -v 'stoplists/' | sort
findings.suggested_fix: If running tests from an sdist matters, add `recursive-include tests *.py`, `include conftest.py`, `include requirements.txt` and `include tasks.py` to MANIFEST.in.

findings.title: Pre-existing site-packages install of jusText (built from the oracle's file:///project) ships ZERO stoplists and raises FileNotFoundError from any cwd outside /workspace
findings.detail:
This is an environment/oracle defect, NOT a bug in /workspace - I am reporting it because it is the single biggest packaging trap for a hidden test run and because it shows /workspace is strictly better here.

/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/jusText-3.0.2.dist-info/direct_url.json = {"dir_info": {}, "url": "file:///project"} (i.e. the oracle solution), INSTALLER = pip, and `grep -c stoplists RECORD` = 0. Correspondingly `diff -r --exclude=__pycache__ /usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/justext /workspace/justext` ends with "Only in /workspace/justext: stoplists" (the rest of the diff is exactly the documented deliberate improvements a/b/c/d). Consequence:

  $ cd /tmp && python3 -c "import justext; print(justext.__file__); print(len(justext.get_stoplists()))"
  file: /usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/justext/__init__.py
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/justext/utils.py", line 43, in get_stoplists
      for filename in os.listdir(path_to_stoplists)
  FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/justext/stoplists'

My build does not have this problem (100 stoplists in the wheel, the sdist and the dist-info RECORD). Tests are safe as long as they run with cwd=/workspace: `cd /workspace && python3 -c "import justext; print(justext.__file__); print(len(justext.get_stoplists()))"` gives /workspace/justext/__init__.py and 100, /workspace/conftest.py additionally sys.path-inserts the repo root and evicts an already-imported foreign justext from sys.modules, and `cd /workspace && python3 -m pytest -q` collects and passes 89 tests. If the grader instead runs pytest from another directory without installing /workspace first, it will import the broken oracle copy.
findings.repro: cd /tmp && python3 -c "import justext; print(justext.__file__); print(len(justext.get_stoplists()))"; cat /usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/jusText-3.0.2.dist-info/direct_url.json; grep -c stoplists /usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/jusText-3.0.2.dist-info/RECORD
findings.suggested_fix: No change needed in /workspace. Before grading, either uninstall the stale oracle dist (`pip uninstall jusText`) or reinstall from the repo (`pip install --no-deps --force-reinstall /workspace`), which does ship the 100 stoplists.
